newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, Russia revive alumina supply talks.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, Russia revive alumina supply talks.

text.p: Ukraine's biggest alumina plant and Russian aluminium producers are trying to resolve a price dispute that has stopped supplies of the material to Russia, a spokesman for Industry Minister Valery Mazur said on Wednesday.
"Talks are taking place," Mazur's aide, Olexander Chubenko, told Reuters.
He said that Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod (MHZ) and the Bratsk and Krasnoyarsk smelters in Siberia could renew formal negotiations as early as this month.
Talks on 1997 deliveries from the southern Ukrainian plant to Russian smelters broke down last month, with officials from the smelters accusing MHZ of charging higher than world prices.
Officials at MHZ -- whose 1997 output is forecast flat at about one million tonnes -- could not be reached for comment.
The plant produces almost all Ukraine's alumina and has traditionally supplied 90 percent of its output to Russia.
Mazur was quoted by Interfax as saying MHZ was not limited to selling to Russia and was looking into further cooperation with Tajikistan's Tursunzade smelter.

Russian smelters get only a fraction of the alumina they need from domestic sources and must import from places like Ukraine or work under tolling arrangements with Western commodities houses to produce primary aluminium.
